chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Don't Be Afraid, The Clown's Afraid Too and Let My Children Hear Music
summary: Johnson on transcribing the Monterey pieces; Mingus on writing the multi-line French horn theme, the 15-measure section.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, why don't you say something about those pieces, because -- "Don't Be Afraid, The Clown's Afraid, Too," and the piece that eventually became "The Shoes of the Fisherman's Wife." You had another title at that point.
Yeah, it was --
A Holding Corporation Called Old America, right.
"Once Upon a Time. . ."
You're right, yeah.
"There was a Holding Corporation. . ."
And those are superb pieces, and --
It was a good band.

It was not only a good band, it was good writing. You wrote -- you sat down and really wrote some ambitious and beautiful music. And when it came to do that for the -- Let My Children Hear Music album and you gave me those tapes to work on, they were a pleasure to do. I mean, as

hard as some of that was to take off the tapes, they were -- the music was so linear. I mean, all the lines were so clear and distinct and everything shaped itself so beautifully, that I remember thinking to myself that what I have to do on this date is to make this music sing, just take the music as there and make it -- use everything I know to make all those beautiful lines sing and glisten.

And I tried very hard to do that. And -- but, like, "Don't Be Afraid, The Clown is Afraid, Too," there's about seven lines in that, going on at the same time, at the beginning of that, and maybe you could just say something about how you happened to write that.
I don't know.
You don't know.
I enjoyed it. I -- if I write something, I usually hear what I do, at the time.
No, I know you do.
In a trance. Even if I can't play it myself.
Well, there's no way you can play that by yourself. I mean, you need about four more hands in order to be able to play that by yourself. But I presume you started with the part --
(Singing.) I started with that line.
The part that the --
French horn.
French horn, yeah. And the tuba had. Yeah, that's what I thought. That seems to be the natural place to start, and then you added the other lines on top of that. It's just beautiful.

You said something very interesting to me that time. I called you up, we were talking every day, and I was going over to your apartment. I called you up and asked you, I just happened to mention in passing that that had 15 measures to it, that section of it was 15 measures long. And you very seriously considered writing another measure to make it come out to 16. You said, 'I think I'll write another measure on that.' And I said, 'You don't have to. Geez, it really is all complete.' You said, 'Really? Is it only 15 measures? Is that all it is?'
I (inaudible) measures a long time ago.
I know, but it's just as well off.
